# Premortem: Codex-Ratchet Merge-Base Failure

## THE FAILURE STORY

On merge day, when the team attempted to consolidate the 43 unmerged commits across the 10 worktrees back into origin/main, git's three-way merge algorithm silently used the wrong ancestor. Each worktree had been created from claimgate/bypass-regression (6e362506a), but origin/main had advanced beyond that point (a9909489 is 6,637 lines of scaffolding commits ahead). The automatic merge-base detection should have found the true common ancestor, but instead it used 6e362506a as the baseline—the very point from which the worktrees had split.

This meant that when consolidating changes from system_v5 and system_v7 worktrees, the three-way merge algorithm couldn't see that certain refactorings in main had already happened. Code that bridged the system boundaries—the "boundary scaffolding" keeping v5 and v7 wired together—was already present in main but invisible to the merge logic. When a worktree had touched the same code, the conflict resolution marked it as a deletion. Developers, seeing this as a normal conflict in the busy v5/v7 boundary files, used `git merge --ours` to resolve in favor of main, which actually discarded the worktree's improvements while keeping main's version of the scaffolding. But six months later in production, when the system tried to execute the boundary-glue logic at runtime, it failed: the scaffolding had been left intact but the actual wiring code that called it had been silently dropped during merge.

## THE UNDERLYING ASSUMPTION

The team assumed claimgate/bypass-regression would remain a valid merge-base for all ten worktrees against an advancing origin/main without needing explicit verification.

## EARLY WARNING SIGNS

1. **Merge conflict density spike**: System_v5 and system_v7 boundary files showed an unusually high conflict rate during the merge—entire functions marked as both added and deleted in the same files.

2. **Unran verification**: No one ran `git diff <merge-result> <expected-state>` to confirm the merged files actually contained all the wiring code that should have been present.
